ch17.b.d.f1: Frequency of the first sound wave
ch17.b.d.df: Frequency $f_2$ of the second wave minus $f_1$
ch17.b.d.sound: Play both tones together at their real frequencies (needs speakers; 20 Hz is barely audible)
ch17.b.goal.sum: Two waves of slightly different frequency add up to a wave whose amplitude rises and falls periodically (beats)
ch17.b.goal.fbeat: Beat frequency $f_\text{beat} = \lvert f_1 - f_2 \rvert$: how many times per second the sound swells
ch17.b.obs.phase: $y_1$ and $y_2$ start in phase, drift apart, and after $1/(2\Delta f)$ are exactly out of phase
ch17.b.obs.env: Sum $y$: amplitude $2A$ when in phase, 0 when out of phase. Grey dashed = envelope
ch17.b.obs.df: Frequency difference 1 → 4 Hz: beat period 1 s → 0.25 s. Changing $f_1$ leaves the beat period unchanged
ch17.b.obs.arrows: Arrows above: the two amplitudes drift apart and back together at $f_2 - f_1$; the black arrow's length is the envelope
ch17.b.obs.sound: Sound on with $f_1$ = 440 Hz: the tone swells and fades as many times per second as the frequency difference
ch17.b.assume.amp: Both waves have the same amplitude ($A = 1$, arbitrary units)
ch17.b.assume.slow: Graphs are drawn at 1/4 of real speed; the sound plays at the real frequencies
ch17.b.assume.arrows: Arrows above: the two amplitudes seen in a frame turning at the mean frequency $(f_1 + f_2)/2$
ch17.b.assume.env: When $f_1$ is so high that a cycle is too short to resolve on the plot, each wave is drawn as the band between its envelopes
ch17.d.d.who: The source moves (observers at rest) or the observers move (source at rest)
ch17.d.d.vs: Speed of the source moving to the right; the speed of sound is 340 m/s
ch17.d.d.vo: Both observers move left together: A towards the source, B away from it
ch17.d.goal.source: When the source or the observer moves, the heard frequency changes: higher when approaching, lower when receding
ch17.d.goal.mach: A source faster than sound piles its wavefronts into a cone: a shock wave (Mach cone)
ch17.d.obs.spacing: Moving source: fronts are crowded ahead (towards A) and spread out behind (towards B)
ch17.d.obs.count: An observer's ring flashes black when a front arrives; flashes per second = heard frequency
ch17.d.obs.v: Source speed 340 m/s (equal to the speed of sound): the fronts ahead all pile up on the source; no sound reaches A ahead of it
ch17.d.obs.cone: Source speed 510 m/s: Mach cone with half-angle $\sin\theta = v/v_S = 0.67$
ch17.d.obs.observer: Moving observers: the fronts stay concentric; A, moving towards the source, meets them more often, B less often
ch17.d.assume.medium: Still air, speed of sound $v = 340\ \text{m/s}$, source frequency $f = 100\ \text{Hz}$ (wavelength 3.4 m). One front is drawn per period
